device.description: 12-bit single-channel voltage-output DAC with I2C interface and power-down
device.note: dac7571.pdf (SLAS374D) p.2 pin configuration and pin description (SOT23-6), p.3-4 electrical characteristics (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic inputs), p.4-5 I2C timing, p.15-16 I2C interface, address byte (1001 10 A0 0, broadcast 1001 0000), Figure 45 Ctrl/MS-byte and LS-byte, p.17 write sequence (Table 1), power-on reset (zero), p.18 modes of operation (Table 2)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: p.17: power-on fills the DAC register with zeros

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: PD1/PD0 of the Ctrl/MS-byte (Table 2): 0 normal, 1 1k to AGND, 2 100k to AGND, 3 Hi-Z

commands.name: Write Ctrl/MS-byte + LS-byte
commands.note: Table 1 / Figure 45: 0 0 PD1 PD0 D11-D8, D7-D0; byte pairs repeat until STOP; conversion at the ACK after the LS-byte

pages: p.2 (pinout), p.3-4 (VDD, logic levels), p.4-5 (I2C timing), p.15-17 (I2C protocol, address byte, data bytes, Table 1), p.17-18 (power-on reset, power-down modes, Table 2)
notModeled: analog output, settling and power-down output loads (PD bits stored only; the output is never driven)
broadcast address 1001 0000 (responds regardless of A0): not expressible in the address table
address pin A0 is latched at power-up (the model reads it live)
I2C high-speed mode master code and timing limits
a Ctrl/MS-byte whose two top bits are not 0 0 is dropped (the datasheet only defines 0 0)
receive-only interface: a read (R/W = 1) is not acknowledged by the part; the model's read behaviour is the engine default
variants: DAC7571 has its own datasheet; DAC5571 (8-bit) and DAC6571 (10-bit) are the same family with narrower data fields
